flags.quote: Score 10: exactly on the threshold. One more clue and it goes to junk; one fewer and it reaches the inbox.
flags.problem: The rule used everywhere else (bh.rule, cmp.explain, ch, post1.fb, an.f1 'at least') is 'threshold or more goes to junk', so a score of exactly 10 already goes to junk. This text says one more clue is needed to reach junk. The same error is in the hi and te versions.
flags.why: It contradicts the lesson's own rule at the exact boundary case the learner has just built, and teaches a wrong reading of 'reaches the threshold'. It can leave a learner unsure whether 10 is junk or inbox.
flags.fix: Rewrite: 'Score 10: exactly on the threshold, and 10 is enough to go to junk. Take away even one point and it reaches the inbox.' Update hi and te to match.

flags.quote: Write up to five messages that you think would fool this filter.
flags.problem: Minors type free text (up to 5 x 120 characters; up to 12 in classroom mode) with no instruction to avoid real personal details (names, phone numbers, addresses, copied real messages). Nothing states that the text is kept on the device only or is not shown on the shared classroom screen. The examples themselves model asking for an address.
flags.why: Article 10: no personal data from children, and nothing personal on a shared classroom screen. Free text from teens is a likely route for personal data or for real people's messages to be shown to a class.
flags.fix: Add a plain line: 'Make them up. Don't use real names, numbers, addresses or messages from real people.' Confirm and state that entries stay on the learner's device. For classroom mode, show only anonymous, teacher-moderated entries, or counts.

flags.quote: Nobody sets their points by hand: the filter works them out from millions of messages
flags.problem: The absolute 'Nobody' is false. Many rule-based filters (for example SpamAssassin-style systems) have hand-tuned scores, and many filters combine learned and hand-set rules. 'Hundreds of clues' also understates modern systems. No source is given.
flags.why: A simplification that becomes a falsehood (Article 11).
flags.fix: Say 'Most modern filters don't have their points set by hand: they work them out from very large numbers of messages that people marked as junk.' Soften 'hundreds' to 'many hundreds or more'. Add a source in the notes.

flags.quote: क्रिकेट अभ्यास शुक्रवार को हो गया है
flags.problem: The English source is 'practice moved to Friday'. The Hindi says 'cricket practice has happened on Friday'. The meaning of a schedule change is lost and the tense is wrong.
flags.why: The message is meant to be a plainly real message. A different meaning changes what the learner is sorting.
flags.fix: Use 'क्रिकेट अभ्यास अब शुक्रवार को होगा' or similar, checked by a native speaker.

flags.problem: English is 'Meeting moved to 3 pm'. 'हो गई है' reads as 'the meeting has already happened', and the text does not say 3 pm.
flags.why: The wrong meaning makes the example ambiguous and does not match the English source.

flags.problem: The item's shared symbol is a cricket bat, but the English label says football. The hi and te labels say cricket, so the symbol only fits those.
flags.why: A symbol that contradicts the label confuses learners, and screen readers may announce the emoji name.
flags.fix: Make the symbol locale-specific (⚽ for en), or use a neutral icon. Mark symbols as decorative for assistive technology.

flags.quote: उन लाखों संदेशों से / లక్షలాది సందేశాల నుండి
flags.problem: English says 'millions'. 'लाखों' and 'లక్షలాది' mean hundreds of thousands (lakhs).
flags.fix: Use 'करोड़ों / కోట్లాది', or change all locales to a looser phrase such as 'a very large number'.

flags.quote: hi and te are unreviewed drafts
flags.problem: The hi and te strings have not been reviewed by native speakers (localeStatus is draft). Factual claims about filters ('Early filters worked a lot like that', 'real filters use hundreds of clues') have no source recorded.
flags.why: Article 11 requires native-speaker review of translations and sourced content, and the Hindi errors above show review is needed.
flags.fix: Hold hi and te back from publication until a native-speaker review is done. Record sources for the filter-history and scale claims.
